claims.text: Enhanced dynamic mechanical behavior in high-entropy alloys is caused by local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions hinder dislocation motion during dynamic loading.
Hindered dislocation motion increases strain hardening.
The as-cast or homogenized HEA has inherent local lattice distortions associated with its multiple principal elements.
Atomic-size mismatch and chemical disorder create local lattice distortions.
Atomic-scale distortions act as obstacles to dislocation motion under dynamic loads.
Obstruction of dislocation motion increases the work-hardening rate.
Increased work hardening delays the onset of plastic instability.
Dynamic loading promotes dislocation accumulation without premature strain localization.
The proposed dislocation response produces a favorable balance of strength and ductility.
Under identical dynamic loading, the HEA will have a higher strain-hardening rate than the conventional or reduced-complexity alloy.
Under identical dynamic loading, the HEA will have a more stable stress response, with less pronounced stress drops or strain localization.
After deformation, the HEA will show a higher density of dislocation tangles correlated with regions of severe local distortion.
The conventional or reduced-configurational-entropy control lacks the pronounced lattice distortions of the HEA.
The conventional or reduced-complexity control exhibits lower strain hardening under comparable dynamic loading.
The proposed mechanism applies to HEAs having significant chemical disorder and local lattice distortions.
The proposed mechanism applies at moderate temperatures and high strain rates before thermally activated processes dominate.
Very high temperatures and very slow strain rates may lie outside the regime in which the proposed mechanism controls behavior.
No temporally eligible evidence was provided to support the proposed mechanism.
Failure to observe higher strain hardening or enhanced distortion/dislocation signatures in the HEA relative to the control would falsify the claim that lattice distortions are the primary mediator.
